description:
FOUND s486 (Fable, docs/security-review-s486.md §3).  Measured: `tools/runt lex` -> 53 pass, 0 fail, 8 `# REGISTRY-STALE` lines (tests 11-14 `$/@/%/& <null> ident` + others); `perl tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl` (s486b's run, and B's 24-file measurement) -> lex.t 45/0 with 8 `[registry]` skips and 0 stale; same for join.t (43 vs 41/2 skips) and sub.t (58/0/7 vs 54/2/9).

RULED OUT by measurement (s486): the transpile (`pl2cl --no-cache --lenient-ppi lex.t` from perl-tests/ is byte-identical to runt's /tmp/lex.lisp, cmp); the loader and core (a hand run of the sweep's exact command -- sbcl --core <cached core> --load cl/pcl-test.lisp --load cl/skip-registry.lisp --eval (setf pcl::*current-test-file* "lex.t") --eval (pcl::p-load-with-recovery "/tmp/lex.lisp") from perl-tests/ -- ALSO gives 53/8 stale); PCL_DROP_LOG set or unset (no change); stdin </dev/null (no change).  A `setsid` attempt was invalid (setsid forks; the output file was read before the run finished) -- redo it as `setsid -w`.

NEXT (cheap, ~5 min): run `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 perl tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl --jobs 1 perl-tests/lex.t` and diff (1) the exact command, (2) the %ENV the sweep hands the child (wrap sbcl in a script that dumps `env` to a file), (3) the fresh_perl CHILD's command (tools/pclperl-for-tests, its own transpile of the NUL-bearing child program -- the memory note says --lenient-ppi truncates NUL source, so the CHILD's transpile path is the prime suspect: under runt the child may be reaching a cached module transpile or a different pl2cl flag set).  Until located, a hand run of a fresh_perl file is NOT the sweep's verdict -- s486's own registry-stale count read 19 where the sweep says 7 because of this.
subject: Runner drift: tools/runt and a hand run pass lex.t's four <null>-ident fresh_perl rows (53/0, 8 REGISTRY-STALE) where the sweep fails and registry-relabels them (45/0/8) -- join.t 43 vs 41, sub.t 58/0 vs 54/2; cause NOT located
